summary:
Verdict: redo, on one major item and three minors. The GPU gate is met and every review-2 issue is fixed in the looks the tests measure. The major item: in a real match the per-era lighting never changes at a jump. So the TODAY and 3000s dusks that fix round 2 tuned are never what a player sees. At dusk the 3000s plays washed out to a pale lilac-white.

**What I did.** I edited no source and committed nothing to b5-stage-bluestone. I pushed one scratch job, JOB-27 (bfb4b6b1), to botlab-b5-bluestone; its results are on that branch. I then removed my temporary worktree. Local runs went one Electron at a time under SLOTS=3, at load 4–25. I looked at every sheet and picture. They are in SP = /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-danielosling-Desktop-1/dd09cb28-6f60-4591-8992-4f7ec6fb49a8/scratchpad/art3, with the sheets in SP/sheets/, the sweep pages in SP/ov/ and the logs in SP/logs/ and SP/mm/JOB-27.raw.txt.

**What holds, re-measured at 866e11ec:**
- **Play geometry is frozen.**
  - The check-maps output is identical to review 2 for bluestone, .tower, .zones, .bazookarp and .boss: 712 / 706 / 712 / 762 / 710 pieces, and 568 / 590 / 700 per era.
  - The layout.js diff touches only ERAS.look, the tint and levelTexlib. No props were added on walkable tops or as colliders.
  - climb-audit: 144 climbs, 0 barred, in every era.
  - cover-map: floor cells 5006 / 5166 / 5688; 99.6 / 99.6 / 99.5 % within 5 m; largest open circle 7 m.
  - tower-check: 73.99 m, no holes, clearance clean, in every era. spawn-mid passes in every era.
- **The engine's tests pass (JOB-27, Mac mini, load 1.4).**
  - eras-static 23/23; eras-world 12/12, 7/7 and 3/3; eras-look 20/20.
  - eras-jump: first 1/1; a 8/8, b 7/7, c 3/3, e 6/6; frames 4/4 three times (worst jump frame 31.9 / 11.1 / 34.5 ms).
  - eras-hud 12/12, eras-modes 6/6, stage-mods 36/36, world-build 5/5 on both stages.
  - The 421 ms stall did not recur.
- **The bake applies everywhere.** eras-bake 3/3. stage-audit turf, zones and tower in eras 1–3 and boss in era 2 all say "lightmap applied (baked for this build, not stale)".
- **Performance is level with Halyard (perf6, 3 runs):** draw calls ×0.81–1.01, triangles ×0.40–0.46, CPU render time ×0.77–0.83.
- **The GPU gate (method C) is met.** By era (day / dusk): 1880s ×0.86 / ×0.90, TODAY ×0.89 / ×0.91, 3000s ×0.91 / ×0.95. Halyard is 7.12 / 7.27 ms.
- **Online:** net-eras 13/14. On the Iron Bridge, 2 of 368 cells differed on every try in the flip window; JOB-25 passed 14/14 with the same source. The lead already ruled this beta round 2, not an art gate. The lagged run passed 8/8.
- **Turf War 3:00 ERAS lines:** 0 shoves, 0 rescues, 52 flips, 0 players on a vanishing top or inside an appearing piece, 0 splats caused by a jump. Stuck 0 %, console 0, frame errors 0. Bots reached jump 1's new ground 2/8 within 30 s and jump 2's 6/8 (median 14.4 s).

**The judgement:**
- **The city does change at street level as the front passes**, not only the skyline. The arcade's hoardings become shopfronts and then pearl glass. The kiosk, tram, signs, kerbs, lamps, clocks, iron and paving all switch along one clean white-gold line, with the Roman-numeral curtain riding it. No 20 cm blocks remain, and it reads as a showpiece, not a glitch (SP/sheets/jump1-swimston-day.jpg, jump2-swimston-day.jpg, jump*-knee-*.jpg).
- **The eight places, same camera in all three eras**, show three distinct streets, by day and at rest at dusk (SP/sheets/places-*-day/dusk.jpg). Bravo's twins match Alpha's in all 12 sweeps; console 0 in every sweep.
- **Team ink is the loudest colour** in every era, day and dusk, in the looks the tests measure. In the lower two thirds of the frame, background pixels at least as saturated as the ink are ≤ 0.54 %, against Halyard's ≤ 1.52 %. Tangerine-like background is ≤ 3.5 %, against Halyard's 22–43 %.
- **Review 2's issues are resolved in those looks:**
  1. The GPU gate is met (issue 1).
  2. At rest, the dusk 'mid' preset's lower-frame median is 43 / 48 / 50, against Halyard's 49 (issue 2).
  3. The trams are a low-floor tram with panes, doors, the destination blind "11 FLOUNDERS ST" and fleet number 6012, and a glass float-tram (issue 3).
  4. The cards now show a dressed city (SP/sheets/cards-vs-halyard.jpg) (issue 4).
  5. The drum ceiling is coffered per era, with no seam (issue 5).
  6. Cobalt reads in the 3000s dusk at rest (issue 6).
  7. The 3000s furniture, the monument, and the fountain, buffer and rails per era are done (issue 7).
- **Issue 8 still has no decision** recorded in LEAD-NOTES.

**What fails:**
1. **(major)** The era's lighting is applied only by debugJump and seek, never by a real jump. Every dusk test, sweep and picture, mine included, measured a look that matches never reach.
2. **(minor)** The procedural pseudo-lettering reads as rows of placeholder blocks at eye level.
3. **(minor)** Several 1880s and TODAY cover pieces are still plain boxes.
4. **(minor, the lead's)** The carried items.

issues.title: In a real match the era's lighting never changes at a jump: matches show TODAY and the 3000s at dusk under the 1880s' lights (the 3000s washed out to a pale lilac-white), and the tests, sweeps and earlier pictures all measured the debugJump look instead
issues.evidence:
**The lights after a real jump (SP/logs/lights-dusk.log).** A match started at dusk keeps the 1880s sunset's lights:
- At start (1880s): sun 3.5 #ffe6c8, hemisphere light 2.1 #8a84b8, environment light 1.2, exposure 1.2.
- After the real jump 1 (done + 5 s, TODAY): the same values.
- After the real jump 2 (done + 5 s and done + 30 s, 3000s): the same values.

Only a debugJump to another era applies that era's own look:
- TODAY: sun 3.9 #ffd4bc, hemisphere 2.2, environment 0.75, exposure 1.08, shadow tint (0.88, 0.96, 1.16).
- 3000s: sun 3.2 #fff2e2, hemisphere 0.8, environment 0.3, exposure 1.0.

The sky's clouds and horizon glow also stay the 1880s'. TODAY's pink clouds and pink glow never appear in a match.

**The cause** (src/game/eras.js line 919). The 'env' event runs `W._envEra(J.to, false); this._envFinal(J)`. `_envFinal` sets only the zenith, sky middle, horizon, haze, sun direction, cloud rate, fog and the env map. It never sets:
- sun.color / sun.intensity;
- uSunLight;
- the hemisphere sky, ground and intensity;
- scene.environmentIntensity;
- env.grade (exposure and tints);
- uGround, the horizon glow, uSunDisk, the cloud lit/shade colours and bake, the stars.

`_envEra(e, true)` → setTheme runs only from apply() (debugJump) and seek() (a late joiner or clock snap). So a late joiner online sees a different city from the players who were there for the jump.

**The tests miss it.** eras-look (g) and every Cobalt or dusk measure enter the era through debugJump. eras-jump 'sky' even asserts `env.grade === grade0` until done + 1.2 s, which locks the bug in.

**Measured, one camera each** (SP/afterjump, SP/tools/ajmetric.py; median of the lower two thirds of the frame, and the share above 200/255).

3000s dusk, real match vs debugJump:

| Place | Real match | debugJump |
|---|---|---|
| Circus | 145, 13.7 % | 72, 5.0 % |
| Knee | 135, 13.4 % | 60, 6.7 % |
| Quay | 111, 19.3 % | 48, 5.1 % |
| Swimston | 150, 26.8 % | (its debugJump shot repeated the quay camera) |

TODAY dusk, real match vs debugJump: 53–102 against 45–92. By day the two are identical, as the day looks share their lights.

**Pictures:**
- SP/sheets/dusk-real-vs-instant.jpg: the left two columns are a real match, the right two debugJump.
- SP/sheets/settle-dusk.jpg: done + 1, + 8 and + 30 s against at rest. It does not settle.
- SP/sheets/jump2-knee-dusk.jpg: the pearl street furniture and the float-tram read as pale blobs.
- SP/sheets/e3dusk-rest-vs-afterjump.jpg.
issues.fix:
**1. Apply the new era's lights in the done-time 'env' event, src/game/eras.js `_envFinal(J)`.**
- Factor the light block of Environment.setTheme (environment.js 3231 ff) into a method, e.g. `env.applyLights(T)`, so setTheme and `_envFinal` share one source of truth.
- `applyLights(T)` sets:
  - `sun.color` / `sun.intensity`;
  - `U.uSunLight` = lin(sunColor, (skySun ?? sunIntensity) / π);
  - `hemi.color` / `hemi.groundColor` × hemiGroundK / `hemi.intensity`;
  - `scene.environmentIntensity = T.envK ?? 0.66`;
  - `this.grade = T.grade`;
  - `U.uGround`, `uHorizonGlow`, `uGlowColor`, `uGlowParams`, `uSunDisk`, `uCloudLit`, `uCloudShade`, `uNight` and the stars.
- Call it from `_envFinal` with `B.Tt`. Re-bake the clouds only if cloudLit or cloudShade differ, or blend them through the time-lapse with the sky colours.
- Better still: blend sun, hemisphere and environment intensity, and the exposure, from the old era's values to the new ones over done → done + 0.7 s, so the light does not pop.

**2. Correct eras-jump 'sky'.**
- Hold exposure and the grade from J to done only.
- After the env event, assert the grade's values equal the target era theme's. Compare values: setTheme makes a new object on every call.

**3. Add a real-jump test (eras-look part 5 (i)).**
- Start a match at dusk and run the clock through both jumps with no debugJump.
- At done + 2 s, assert env.sun.intensity, hemi.intensity, scene.environmentIntensity and grade.uExposure equal a debugJump to that era.
- Re-run (g)'s lower-frame median and Cobalt share in that state.

**4. Online.** seek() and the done path must give the same look, so a late joiner matches the room.

**5. Re-shoot** SP's dusk-real-vs-instant pair. Re-measure the dusk 'mid' preset after a real jump; it must reach ≥ 40, as at rest, with the 3000s' lower-frame share above 200/255 ≤ 7 %. Re-run the ink pairs after a real jump.

issues.title: Most shop fascias, booth boards, kiosk boards and cart and bin labels are procedural pseudo-lettering that reads as rows of placeholder blocks at eye level
issues.evidence:
**The lettering function.** src/world/stages/bluestone/levelart.js `bsText()` (line 187) draws letter-shaped bars with random gaps and counters, not letters. It is used for:
- the shop fascias (line 561);
- the civic signs (594);
- the shelter and room boards (496, 504);
- the cover pieces' labels.

From 2–6 m it reads as "▯▯▯▯ ▯▯".

**Pictures:**
- SP/sheets/zoom-lettering.jpg: the arcade fascia and the hanging plaques.
- SP/sheets/places-A2-day.jpg: the forecourt booth by the spawn, in every era.
- SP/ov/e2-day-02.jpg and SP/ov/e3-day-00.jpg: the ticket booths, cart, bins and coal bin.

**The contrast.** The hero names are real lettering: THE ROYAL ARCADE, GPO, SWIMSTON ST, TELEPHONE, CUSTOMS HOUSE, FLOAT-TRAM DOCK, STATION. Halyard's signs are real words throughout.
issues.fix:
**Real words on what a player reads up close.** Draw them through the mural/sign atlas that already renders the street plates (murals.js):
- Each arcade and Swimston shop's fascia name per era, matching its room's trade: CHOCOLATIER, TOYS, BARBER, CAFE, BOOKS, FLORIST, OUTFITTER, in gilt, painted and light lettering.
- The ticket booths: TICKETS / BOOKING OFFICE, then MYKI-style TOP UP, then a 3000s light panel.
- The forecourt booth.
- The kiosk boards.
- The bins: CITY OF … / RECYCLE.

**Elsewhere,** keep `bsText` only where the text is under about 12 px tall on screen from the nearest walkable point (far facades and upper storeys). Or replace it with a plain moulded fascia panel.

**Then** re-run the e1–e3 day sweeps and look at the booth, cart, bins and arcade-wall pages.

issues.title: Several 1880s and TODAY cover pieces still read as plain rounded boxes at eye level: the fountain, the horse trough, the Hoki Lane bin, the coal bin and the bollard blocks
issues.evidence:
**At eye level (the sweep's own cameras):**
- **Prow Place's drinking fountain** (1880s and TODAY): a grey granite box with two brass roundels. There is no basin rim, bowl, spout, water or pedestal (SP/sheets/sweep-small-cover-e123.jpg row 1; SP/sheets/places-D2-day.jpg row 1).
- **The horse trough** (1880s): a grey rounded box with two dark panels and no trough lip or water (sweep-small-cover-e123.jpg row 2).
- **The Hoki Lane bin** (1880s): a featureless blue-grey rounded box (row 4).
- **The coal bin** on the wharf (1880s and TODAY): a matte black box (SP/sheets/sweep-small-cover-e123-b.jpg row 3).
- **The bollard blocks** (1880s): grey boxes with rings (sweep-small-cover-e123.jpg row 3).

**The 3000s versions** of the same pieces were dressed in fix round 2 (pearl family, a fountain of light, a buffer of light).
